newsitem.title: CHINA: China ethylene plant starts trial production.
newsitem.headline: China ethylene plant starts trial production.

text.p: An ethylene plant in China's southern province of Guangdong began trial production this week to help meet rising ethylene demand in the region, state-owned China National Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) said on Friday.

The Maoming plant was expected to produce 300,000 tonnes of ethylene a year capable of making 890,000 tonnes of synthethic resin, chemical fibre and organic chemical materials, a Sinopec official said by telephone.
Sinopec holds a 60 percent stake in the project and the Guangdong provincial government holds the remaining, the official said.
The plant is located in the industrial hub of Maoming city and cost 17.7 billion yuan ($2.1 billion) to build, the official China Daily said.
Construction of the plant began in November 1993 with two-thirds of the cost shouldered by foreign investors, the newspaper said but did not give further details.
The plant was expected to generate annual revenues of seven billion yuan and taxes totalling 1.6 billion yuan, the newspaper said without elaborating.
Maoming is also home to China's largest oil refinery.

Another ethylene plant was under construction in neighbouring Guangzhou, provincial capital of Guangdong, the newspaper said. The 145,000-tonne ethylene project was expected to start operation by the end of 1996.
